ra: The lwa serve and mediate the remote creator Bondye, who is their ultimate source (Métraux; Murphy).
Rada is one of the principal nanchon (divisions) of the lwa.
Petwo is one of the principal nanchon (divisions) of the lwa.
Papa Legba is a lwa.
Legba is served as a Rada lwa, saluted first in ceremony (Métraux).
Erzulie Freda Dahomey is a Rada lwa of love and beauty (Murphy).
Erzulie Dantor is the fierce Petwo counterpart of Erzulie (Murphy).
The Petwo Dantor and Rada Freda form the documented hot/cool polarity of the Erzulie complex (Murphy).
Damballa Wedo is the senior Rada serpent lwa (Métraux).
Ayida-Wedo is a Rada serpent lwa (Métraux).
Ayida-Wedo and Damballa are the paired rainbow/serpent consorts (Métraux).
Baron Samedi heads the Gede family of death lwa (Murphy).
The Gede are a family/nanchon within the lwa.
Maman Brigitte is a Gede lwa of the cemetery (Murphy).
Maman Brigitte is the documented consort of Baron Samedi (Murphy).
Ogou (Yoruba-derived Ogun) is a lwa of iron and war served across nanchon (Murphy).
Agwe, sovereign of the sea, is a Rada lwa (Métraux).
La Sirène, the mermaid sea spirit, is a lwa (Métraux).
La Sirène is paired with Agwe in the marine complex of lwa (Métraux).
The Marassa (divine twins) are among the lwa served (Murphy).
Loko is a Rada lwa, patron of the priesthood (Métraux).
Simbi, the Kongo-derived water lwa, is a lwa often served in Petwo (Métraux).
Simbi is frequently served within the Petwo nanchon (Métraux).
Papa Legba, keeper of the gates, is popularly identified with St Peter (the keys) in Vodou chromolithography (Métraux; Murphy).
In some lineages the aged, crutch-bearing Legba is imaged as St Lazarus (Métraux).
St Anthony of Padua is also documented as a chromolithographic image for Legba in parts of Haiti (Métraux).
Erzulie Freda is popularly identified with the Mater Dolorosa / Our Lady of Sorrows (Murphy; Métraux).
Erzulie Dantor is popularly imaged as the Black Madonna of Częstochowa (Murphy).
St Barbara also appears among the Catholic images associated with the fierce Erzulie Dantor in Vodou practice (Murphy).
Ogou is popularly identified with St James the Greater (Santiago, the mounted warrior) (Murphy; Métraux).
The divine twins Marassa are popularly imaged as Sts Cosmas and Damian, the holy twin physicians (Murphy; Métraux).
